article.title: Why a Good Propensity-Score Model Is Not Necessarily a Good Causal Model
article.why: Distinguish treatment prediction from causal adjustment quality.

paragraphs.en:
Propensity scores are often estimated with a classification model, so it is tempting to evaluate them like an ordinary prediction problem. Analysts may compare AUC, accuracy, or log loss and choose the model that predicts treatment assignment best. But the goal of a propensity-score model is different from the goal of a marketing response model. Its main job is to support a credible comparison between treated and untreated observations after adjustment.

The propensity score is the probability of receiving treatment conditional on observed covariates. In an observational study, we use it because treatment groups may differ systematically before treatment. Weighting, matching, or stratification attempts to make the groups more comparable on those measured covariates. Therefore, a useful diagnostic is not simply whether the model predicts treatment well, but whether adjustment produces acceptable covariate balance.

A very high AUC can even be a warning sign. Suppose treatment is assigned almost deterministically: premium members nearly always receive a campaign and ordinary members almost never do. A classifier can distinguish treatment extremely well. Yet causal comparison becomes difficult because premium treated customers have few comparable untreated customers. The model’s predictive success reflects separation between groups, which can correspond to poor overlap and extreme weights.

This does not mean that AUC is useless. It can reveal how strongly treatment assignment depends on observed variables, and model fit still matters. A badly misspecified propensity model may fail to balance important confounders. The mistake is treating predictive discrimination as the final objective. For causal adjustment, diagnostics after fitting are essential.

Start by checking standardized mean differences for important covariates before and after weighting or matching. Then inspect propensity-score distributions by treatment group to assess overlap. Examine the weight distribution, including high percentiles and maximum values, because a few extreme weights can dominate an estimate. Effective sample size can show how much information remains after unequal weighting. Segment-level checks are useful when assignment rules differ across customer types.

Variable selection also follows a different logic from pure prediction. A variable that strongly predicts treatment but has little relationship with the outcome can improve treatment prediction while worsening weight variability. Conversely, a confounder that modestly predicts treatment but strongly predicts the outcome may be important for bias reduction. Analysts should use subject-matter knowledge and a causal framework rather than selecting variables only because they increase AUC.

Another distinction is between propensity score and outcome prediction. A propensity model estimates treatment assignment, not the probability that a customer will purchase. Nor does it directly estimate the treatment effect. After adjustment, the causal estimand still depends on assumptions such as exchangeability, positivity, consistency, and correct measurement of relevant confounders. A sophisticated classifier cannot repair unmeasured confounding by itself.

A practical model-review statement could be: ‘The propensity model has moderate discrimination, but after weighting all priority covariates have SMD below the agreed threshold and overlap is adequate.’ That is more informative for causal analysis than saying only, ‘AUC is 0.91.’

The broader lesson is that model quality must be judged against the decision the model serves. Prediction asks whether we can forecast treatment assignment. Causal adjustment asks whether we can create a credible comparison for the target estimand. Those goals overlap, but they are not identical.
paragraphs.zh:
Propensity score 通常透過分類模型估計，因此很容易把它當成一般 prediction problem 評估。分析者可能比較 AUC、accuracy 或 log loss，然後選擇最能預測 treatment assignment 的模型。但 propensity-score model 的目的與行銷 response model 不同；它最重要的工作，是在 adjustment 後支援 treatment 與 untreated observations 之間可信的比較。

Propensity score 是在已觀測 covariates 條件下接受 treatment 的機率。在 observational study 中使用它，是因為 treatment groups 在介入前可能就存在系統性差異。Weighting、matching 或 stratification 試圖讓兩組在這些已測量 covariates 上更可比。因此真正有用的診斷不只是模型能否預測 treatment，而是 adjustment 後 covariate balance 是否達到可接受程度。

非常高的 AUC 甚至可能是警訊。假設 treatment 幾乎由規則決定：premium members 幾乎一定收到 campaign，一般會員幾乎永遠不會收到。Classifier 可以非常準確地區分 treatment，但 causal comparison 反而困難，因為 premium treated customers 幾乎沒有可比較的 untreated customers。模型的預測成功反映兩組高度分離，這往往對應 poor overlap 與 extreme weights。

這並不是說 AUC 完全沒用。它可以顯示 treatment assignment 多大程度依賴觀測變數，模型 fit 仍然重要；錯誤指定的 propensity model 也可能無法平衡重要 confounders。真正的錯誤，是把 predictive discrimination 當成最終目標。因果 adjustment 在模型 fitting 後仍必須做診斷。

首先檢查 weighting 或 matching 前後重要 covariates 的 standardized mean differences。接著看兩組 propensity-score distributions 評估 overlap，再檢查 weight distribution，包括高 percentile 與最大值，因為少數 extreme weights 可能主導估計。Effective sample size 則能顯示不均等 weighting 後還剩多少有效資訊。若不同客群有不同 assignment rules，也應做 segment-level checks。

變數選擇的邏輯也不同於純 prediction。某變數若強烈預測 treatment、卻與 outcome 關係很弱，可能提高 treatment prediction，卻讓 weight variability 更嚴重。相反地，一個對 treatment 預測力普通、但與 outcome 強相關的 confounder，可能對降低 bias 很重要。因此不應只依 AUC 選變數，而要結合 domain knowledge 與 causal framework。

也要區分 propensity score 與 outcome prediction。Propensity model 估的是 treatment assignment，不是顧客購買機率，也不直接估 treatment effect。Adjustment 後的 causal estimand 仍依賴 exchangeability、positivity、consistency，以及重要 confounders 被正確測量等假設。再高級的 classifier 也不能自行修復 unmeasured confounding。

實務 review 可以說：「Propensity model 的 discrimination 中等，但 weighting 後所有 priority covariates 的 SMD 都低於約定門檻，overlap 也足夠。」這比只說「AUC=0.91」更能支持因果分析。

更廣泛的教訓是，模型品質必須依它服務的決策來評估。Prediction 問的是能否預測 treatment assignment；causal adjustment 問的是能否為 target estimand 建立可信比較。兩個目標有交集，但並不相同。
paragraphs.ja:
propensity scoreは分類モデルで推定することが多いため、通常のprediction problemと同じように評価したくなります。AUC、accuracy、log lossを比較し、treatment assignmentを最もよく当てるモデルを選びたくなります。しかしpropensity-score modelの目的はmarketing response modelとは異なり、adjustment後に処置群と非処置群の信頼できる比較を支えることが主な役割です。

propensity scoreは観測covariatesを条件としたtreatmentを受ける確率です。observational studyでは、介入前からtreatment groupsに系統的差があるため利用します。Weighting、matching、stratificationによって、測定されたcovariates上で両群をより比較可能にします。したがって重要なのはtreatment予測精度だけでなく、adjustment後にcovariate balanceが十分かどうかです。

非常に高いAUCが警告になる場合もあります。例えばpremium memberにはほぼ必ずcampaignを配信し、一般会員にはほぼ配信しないとします。classifierはtreatmentを高精度で識別できますが、premium treated customerに対応するuntreated customerがほとんどいないためcausal comparisonは難しくなります。高い予測性能がgroup separationを表し、poor overlapやextreme weightにつながることがあります。

AUCが無意味ということではありません。treatment assignmentが観測変数にどれほど依存しているかを示し、model fitも重要です。misspecified modelでは重要confounderをbalanceできない可能性があります。ただしpredictive discriminationを最終目的にするのは誤りで、causal adjustmentではfit後の診断が不可欠です。

まずweightingやmatching前後の重要covariatesについてstandardized mean differenceを確認します。次にtreatment群別propensity-score distributionからoverlapを確認します。weight distributionの高percentileや最大値も見ます。少数のextreme weightが推定を支配する可能性があるためです。effective sample sizeは不均等weighting後に残る情報量を示します。assignment ruleがsegmentごとに違うならsegment-level checkも有効です。

変数選択もpure predictionとは論理が異なります。treatmentを強く予測してもoutcomeとの関係が弱い変数は、予測精度を高めながらweight variabilityを悪化させることがあります。一方、treatment予測力が中程度でもoutcomeを強く予測するconfounderはbias reductionに重要かもしれません。AUCだけでなくdomain knowledgeとcausal frameworkを使う必要があります。

propensity scoreとoutcome predictionも区別します。propensity modelはtreatment assignmentを推定するもので、購入確率でもtreatment effectでもありません。adjustment後のcausal estimandもexchangeability、positivity、consistency、重要confounderの適切な測定などの仮定に依存します。高度なclassifierでもunmeasured confoundingを自動的には修復できません。

実務では「propensity modelのdiscriminationは中程度ですが、weighting後はpriority covariatesのSMDが合意した基準以下で、overlapも十分です」と説明できます。「AUCは0.91です」だけより因果分析に有用です。

要するにmodel qualityは、そのモデルが支える目的に照らして評価すべきです。Predictionはtreatment assignmentを予測できるかを問い、causal adjustmentはtarget estimandのために信頼できる比較を作れるかを問います。両者は関連しますが同一ではありません。
